notes: Characters now read the clock instead of guessing at it. The story time was already in every prompt, but it sat near the end of a long system prompt with the whole conversation after it — and a time read that far back gets approximated, which is how a character glancing at the microwave announced 2:34 when the story said 2:32. It is now stated twice: once with the date attached, in the paragraph that places the conversation, and again as the very last thing before the reply is written, in the same trailing note that already keeps replies to the right length and the right mode — put there for exactly this reason, because a model follows what it has just read far more readily than a sentence a thousand tokens back. Both say the same thing plainly: any time named, whether reading a clock, saying how late it is, or working out how long something has taken, must match, and no other time may be invented. The prompt's version carries the full date so there is no ambiguity about which Thursday, while the bar at the top of a chat keeps its short form.
